verdict: Costco's net sales rose 9.1% to $68.2B as comparable sales climbed 7.4% — and with $1.36B of nearly cost-free membership fees on top, profit rose 14% to $2.04B.

segments.name: Net sales
segments.note: Everything sold in the warehouses and online. Comparable sales rose 7.4% (6.7% adjusted for gas prices and currency).

segments.name: Membership fees
segments.note: Annual membership fees — almost pure profit, and the engine of Costco's earnings.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Running the warehouses, paying staff and the back office.

otherDetail: Interest income and other of $148M, less $33M of interest expense.
footerNote: Costco's merchandise costs include buying, freight and shrink (lost or damaged goods) — the direct cost of what's on the shelves.
follow100Note: Membership fees are only $1.95 of every $100 — but they arrive with almost no cost attached, which is why they cover about two-thirds of the $2.92 Costco kept as profit.

takeaways.title: Comparable sales still climbing
takeaways.text: Comparable sales rose 7.4% across the company (6.7% adjusted for gas and currency), and digitally-enabled sales jumped 22.6% — members kept spending in the warehouses and online.

takeaways.title: Membership fees outgrow sales
takeaways.text: Membership fee income rose 13.6% to $1.36B — growing faster than net sales, with no cost of goods attached to it.

takeaways.title: Profit up 14%
takeaways.text: Net income rose to $2.04B ($4.58 per share) from $1.79B a year ago — the usual Costco pattern: thin margins on goods, fat margins on memberships.
